name: American Museum of Natural History
tagline: Dinos, the blue whale, and space — NYC’s classic natural history circuit.

items.label: Tyrannosaurus rex
items.one_liner: The T. rex in the Hall of Saurischian Dinosaurs.

qa_card.question: Were all dinosaurs huge?
qa_card.answer: No — some were small, but the big ones steal the show!

items.label: Akeley Hall of African Mammals
items.one_liner: A freestanding group of eight African elephants, plus 28 habitat dioramas.

qa_card.question: How many elephants stand together in Akeley Hall?
qa_card.answer: Eight — a freestanding group in the hall.

items.label: Rose Center for Earth and Space
items.one_liner: The Hayden Sphere and exhibitions on the 13-billion-year history of the universe.
items.zone: Rose Center for Earth and Space

qa_card.question: What is the giant sphere at the Rose Center called?

items.display_label: Rose Center for Earth and Space

items.label: Gilder Center Insectarium
items.one_liner: The Susan and Peter J. Solomon Family Insectarium in the Gilder Center.

qa_card.question: Where is the Insectarium?
qa_card.answer: In the Richard Gilder Center — the Susan and Peter J. Solomon Family Insectarium.

items.label: Titanosaur
items.one_liner: A 122-foot-long Titanosaur in the Wallach Orientation Center.
items.zone: Miriam and Ira D. Wallach Orientation Center

qa_card.question: How long is the Titanosaur?
qa_card.answer: 122 feet — it is in the Wallach Orientation Center.

items.label: Blue whale
items.one_liner: A 94-foot-long, 21,000-pound model of a blue whale.
items.zone: Irma and Paul Milstein Family Hall of Ocean Life

qa_card.question: How long is the blue whale model?
qa_card.answer: 94 feet long, and it weighs 21,000 pounds.

items.label: Triceratops
items.one_liner: Triceratops in the Hall of Ornithischian Dinosaurs, with Stegosaurus nearby.

qa_card.question: Which dinosaur hall has Triceratops?
qa_card.answer: The Hall of Ornithischian Dinosaurs — Stegosaurus is in that hall too.
